lines.trans: The general just hung up the phone.
And what did our boss say?
He did not accept your resignation report.
Really? Did he refuse to sign it?
He ordered our operation to continue.
Does that mean I won't be fired from service?
You remain a major, Anatoliy.
What a huge relief this is for me!
We are colleagues again now!
I am very glad to work with you.
Then sit down at the surveillance equipment quickly.
We must monitor every step of the candidate.
Our work is only just beginning.
Then let us continue listening to this broadcast.

выгнать.gloss: to kick out, to evict, to drive out

meanings.en: to kick out, to drive out
meanings.note: Expel someone from a place. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гнать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to kick out, to evict, to drive out', paired with 'выгонять'.

examples.text: Для тебя она добрая. А меня она выгонит!
examples.trans: She's kind to you. But she'll kick me out!

examples.trans: Does that mean I won't be fired from service?

examples.trans: Put me through to the general.

examples.text: Генерал Круглов ждёт звонка. Будьте любезны.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

meanings.note: Каждый день = every day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

meanings.note: In an election or for a job. From Latin 'candidatus' ('clothed in white toga', worn by office-seekers in ancient Rome).

examples.trans: He is a candidate for mayor.

meanings.note: professional associate (common gender, declined like feminine)

examples.text: Мой коллега помог мне с отчётом.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чальник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'boss, head' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Commence or get underway. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начаться'.

examples.text: Спасибо, теперь для нас начинается новая жизнь.
examples.trans: Thank you, now a new life begins for us.
Our work is only just beginning.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

meanings.en: relief, ease from tension or pain
meanings.note: State of feeling relieved. Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'легчение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'relief, alleviation' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What a huge relief for us!
He breathed a deep sigh of relief.

examples.text: Какое это огромное облегчение для меня!
examples.trans: What a huge relief this is for me!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('huge, enormous').

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: Остаётся у нас = stays with us. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stay, to remain', paired with 'остаться'.

examples.trans: And the advance stays with us.

meanings.note: A document. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sign', paired with 'подписывать'.

examples.text: Пока всё не подпишешь, не выйдешь.

meanings.en: to put, to place, to lay down
meanings.note: + в/на + accusative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to lay down', paired with 'класть'.

examples.text: В гроб с собой икру не положишь!

meanings.note: Кому-то + infinitive. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order, to command', paired with 'приказывать'.

examples.text: А Клавдия Викторовна приказала сделать ей массаж ног!

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to continue', paired with 'продолжить'.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.

meanings.note: Садитесь = sit down (polite). Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'адиться'). следить.gloss: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on
